simple.meaning: בִּיתָן (bîythân) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a palace (i.e. large house).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Esther 1:5. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בִּיתָן (H1055) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H1055. bithan בִּיתָן noun [masculine] house, palace — absolute הַבִּיתָן Est 7:7-8 , ( הב ׳גִּנַּת ); construct בִּיתַן 1:5 ( ב ׳גִּנַּת הַמֶּלֶךְ ), all garden of ׳בּ ; according to Dieulafoy RŠJ 1888, cclxxvii. throne-room , synonym of apadâna in meaning, but compare אַמֶּדֶן . בֵּית preposition between , see [ בַּיִן ] below בין .

occurrences.englishText: When these days were fulfilled, the king made a seven day feast for all the people who were present in Susa the palace, both great and small, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace.

The king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden. Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.

Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman had fallen on the couch where Esther was. Then the king said, “Will he even assault the queen in front of me in the house?” As the word went out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.
